paper.title: Adaptive Pricing in Insurance: Generalized Linear Models and Gaussian Process Regression Approaches

settings.name_in_paper: Generalized Linear Pricing Model (insurance pricing with GLM demand and log-claims)
unmapped: Actions are prices in an interval [p_l, p_h]; expected revenue r(p) = p E[D(p)] - E[C(p)]
Demand mean h1(a0 + a1 p) and log-claims mean h2(b0 + b1 p) with known link and variance functions (quasi-likelihood GLM); learner knows the link and variance functional forms
Learner observes demand and claims separately (richer than revenue-only bandit feedback)
Martingale-difference errors with bounded conditional variance and bounded gamma-th moment, gamma > 2
settings.definition_quote: We assume that the insurance company knows the functional forms of the first two moments of demand and claims. ... E[D(p_t)] = h_1(a_0 + a_1 p_t), Var(D(p_t)) = sigma_1^2 v_1(E[D(p_t)]) ... E[log C(p_t)] = h_2(b_0 + b_1 p_t)

unmapped: Revenue r(p) = p f_d(p) - f_c(p) with f_d, f_c independent GP samples (additive kernel p^2 k_d + k_c)
Learner observes demand and claims separately
settings.definition_quote: Functions f_d(\cdot), f_c(\cdot) are independently sampled from GPs with known means \mu_d, \mu_c and kernels k_d(p,p'), k_c(p,p'). ... r(p_t) = p_t f_d(p_t) - f_c(p_t) + \varepsilon_t^r

settings.name_in_paper: Adaptive GLM Pricing with Unknown Delays (delayed claims)
unmapped: Only claims are delayed (demand observed immediately); delays i.i.d., independent of prices and claims, bounded by maximum waiting time m
GLM demand / log-claims model with known link and variance functions, prices in [p_l, p_h]
settings.definition_quote: We assume that demands are generated and observed immediately when a price is chosen, while claims might be delayed. ... We assume that (\tau_t)_{t \geq 1} is an i.i.d. sequence and is independent of prices and claims. ... Assume there is a maximum waiting time m

bound.expression_latex: \regret(T) = O\left(L_{1}(T)+ \sum_{t=1}^{T} \frac{\log(t)}{L_{1}(t)}\right), L_1(t) = c\sqrt{t\log t} \Rightarrow O(\sqrt{T\log T})

conditions: lambda_min(t) >= L_1(t) = c sqrt(t log t) a.s. for all t >= t_0
unique optimal price with zero first derivative and negative second derivative of revenue (Proposition 4.1)

source.label: theorem_GLMBound
source.quote: Suppose there exists $t_{0} \in \N$, if MQLE $\widehat{{\bm{\beta}}}_{t}$ is strongly consistent and following conditions are satisfied: $\lambda_{\min}(t) \geq L_{1}(t) = c \sqrt{t \log(t)}$ a.s. ... then the regret after $T$ time periods is $\regret\,(T) = O \left(L_{1}(T)+ \sum_{t=1}^{T} \frac{\log(t)}{L_{1}(t)} \right)$.

results.notes: Theorem states general form; the paper remarks immediately after that with L_1 = c sqrt(t log t) this gives O(sqrt(T log T)). Conditions are on the algorithm's trajectory, assumed rather than proven. Regret defined via expected revenue -> pseudo-regret.

conditions: Assumption 4.1: sample paths of f_d, f_c a.s. continuously differentiable with sub-Gaussian tail bound on sup of derivatives
f_d, f_c sampled independently from GPs with known means and kernels
tuning: varphi_t = 2 log(2 t^2 pi^2/(3 delta)) + 2 log(t^2)

source.label: theorem_GPBounds

results.notes: Extension of GP-UCB (Srinivas et al.). Holds w.p. 1-delta; the realised sum of r(p*)-r(p_t) is bounded, with functions drawn from GP prior. Dependence on delta hidden in O.

conditions: lambda_min(t) >= L_1(t) = c sqrt(t log t) a.s. for all t >= t_0
delays bounded by maximum waiting time m

source.label: theorem_GLMDelayBound
source.quote: Suppose there exists $t_{0} \in \N$, if MQLE $\widehat{{\bm{\beta}}}_{t}$ is strongly consistent and following conditions are satisfied: ... $\sum_{t=1}^{T} \left\| \bm{p}(t) - \bm{p}(\widehat{{\bm{\beta}}}_{t}) \right\|^2 \leq \left(2m+K\right) L_{1}(T)$ ... The regret bound is $\regret\,(T) = O \left(L_{1}(T)+ \sum_{t=1}^{T} \frac{\log(t)}{L_{1}(t)} \right)$

results.notes: Same form as Theorem 4.1; with L_1 = c sqrt(t log t) this is O(sqrt(T log T)) (paper's conclusion states the delayed bound equals the non-delayed one). Dependence on m hidden in O.
